The fluorescent lights of the 14th floor hummed with the same energy as the panic rising in Dave’s throat. It was Bring Your Pet to Work Day, and Dave had made a catastrophic error in judgment: he had brought Barnaby, his African Grey parrot, instead of his usual, docile goldfish.

Barnaby sat perched on a stack of quarterly reports, his head cocked, one yellow eye fixed on Dave’s trembling hand as he tried to slide a confidential merger document into a drawer.

"Merger," Barnaby squawked, his voice a perfect, gravelly mimicry of Dave’s boss, Mr. Henderson. "Acquisition of the subsidiary. Tax write-off. Boom."

Dave froze. "Barnaby, hush. That’s private."

"Private?" Barnaby tilted his head. "Dave says, 'Don't tell the SEC.' Dave says, 'The numbers are cooked, but the champagne is cold.'"

The office door swung open. It was Linda from HR, holding a plate of cookies. She smiled, then paused, sensing the tension. "Everything okay, Dave? Barnaby seems... chatty."

"Fine! Just... training him," Dave squeaked, lunging to cover the bird’s beak with a sticky note.

"Training?" Linda raised an eyebrow. "He just said, 'Linda’s bonus is tied to my performance review, which is based on how well I hide the embezzlement.'"

Dave’s face drained of color. Barnaby had never heard that phrase. Dave had muttered it to himself in the bathroom mirror three days ago. The bird had been listening.

"Wait," Linda said, her smile vanishing. "Embezzlement?"

"No! He’s lying! He’s a liar! A feathered liar!" Dave shouted, grabbing Barnaby and shoving him into a cardboard box labeled 'Fragile: Office Supplies.'

"Box!" Barnaby yelled from inside. "Dave is hiding the box! Dave is hiding the box!"

Linda pulled out her phone. "I’m calling security. And legal."

"Wait!" Dave pleaded, sweating profusely. "It’s a joke! A prank! Barnaby learned it from a podcast! 'The Daily Grind: A Parrot’s Perspective on Corporate Fraud!'"

Linda didn’t laugh. She hit dial.
